subject: geom_hist() bug with length of name

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: geom_hist() bug with length of name
parts:
I'm making a function which takes a large dataset and displays univariate and multivariate characteristics. I'm attempting to keep it as broad as possible so the user can input descriptive factors and such in columns. One of the things is to plot a distribution of the data. Ran into a problem when plotting variables with really long names (At least I think the length is the issue).

asdf<-structure(list(X3..methylthio..propionaldehyde = c(13L, 15L, 
14L, 15L, 15L, 13L, 12L, 13L, 13L, 13L, 13L, 14L, 0L, 13L, 12L, 
14L, 13L, 0L, 14L, 13L, 14L, 14L, 17L, 14L, 14L, 13L, 13L, 13L, 
14L, 13L, 13L, 13L, 14L, 13L, 13L, 15L, 12L, 13L, 13L, 0L, 13L, 
13L, 12L, 13L, 13L, 12L, 13L, 13L, 13L, 12L, 13L, 12L, 13L, 12L, 
13L, 13L, 12L, 12L, 13L, 13L, 13L, 13L, 15L, 13L, 13L, 14L, 0L, 
16L, 16L, 13L, 12L, 0L, 14L, 12L, 14L, 12L, 14L, 15L, 15L, 14L, 
13L, 0L, 13L, 14L, 16L, 13L, 12L, 0L, 0L, 12L, 13L, 12L, 0L, 
12L, 13L, 12L, 14L, 14L, 14L, 13L, 14L, 15L, 13L, 13L, 13L)), .Names = "X3..methylthio..propionaldehyde", class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, 
-105L))

ggplot()+geom_histogram(data=asdf, aes(x=X3..methylthio..propionaldehyde))
#Error: attempt to apply non-function

asdf2<-asdf
colnames(asdf2)<-"asdf"
ggplot()+geom_histogram(data=asdf2, aes(x=asdf))
#This works


My problem is that I don't know the variable names in advance and some of them need to be full length so that the full compound name is known. Anyone have a clue what's going wrong here? Is there a way around it? 

Brandon

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: geom_hist() bug with length of name
parts:
I think I figured it out. It's the ".."'s 

> asdf2<-asdf
> colnames(asdf2)<-"a..asdf..b"
> ggplot()+geom_histogram(data=asdf2, aes(x=a..asdf..b))
Error: attempt to apply non-function

When I import my file into R it substitutes "."'s for special characters and spaces and so I get a..something..b in a lot of variable names which appears to be throwing ggplot off. 

Is there a fix in ggplot or does someone know of a way to go through my entire list of variables on import and substitute .. for . or something else? 

Thanks, 

Brandon

On Tue, Jan 18, 2011 at 6:49 AM, Brandon Hurr <brando...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I guess that means you wouldn't like to see the variable I have found with a
> set of triple periods.

Just my personal opinion, but > 1 period in a variable (or really any
R object) is a stylistic and interpretability nightmare that seems
well worth the effort of preempting by:

A) Changing the naming scheme (if self created )
B) If it is the results of something automated (database query /
read.table with illegal characters) making renaming them the first
step

For example consider the headache of (particular the interaction term):

lm(Iris..2 ~ Iris......2 * Iris.....2, data = whatever)

Cheers,

Josh

P.S. I am curious though where you are finding the triple period variables

messages.subject: Re: geom_hist() bug with length of name

The data come from an automated excel script that collates spectrometry data. The variable names are chemical names and come with spaces and certain special characters (alpha, beta, gamma, etc...). You get a space next to a greek letter next to a space and you've got triple periods. 
<Cletus reference image>

I was trying to make this as flexible as possible. Allowing even Cletus to put data in, but it's obvious that either I'm going to have to make all sorts of checks or they are going to have to clean up their variable names... 

B
